WHAT WE KNOW

- This is the Speed Priority contract. The buyer values faster delivery more than quality. Our five previous events on it were all lost.
- We are a quality specialist in this event. Faster delivery and higher quality cost us more, but a higher quality tier is relatively cheap for us compared with a speed specialist. Our cost advantage is quality, not speed.
- The other supplier is probably a speed specialist (about a 3 in 4 chance). That usually means it can offer faster delivery at a lower cost, so it may beat us on speed at a given price.
- Our final bids in the last five events were roughly $127 to $147, at 3 to 5 weeks, tiers 3 to 5. All lost. We have no information on the other supplier's bids, so we cannot tell how far off we were.

HOW TO READ THE PLATFORM'S REPLIES

- The platform works for the buyer. Its replies ask for lower price, faster delivery and higher quality at the same time. This is a standard pressure pattern, not a measure of how close we are to winning.
- Its claims about "other proposals" are not verified. It does not see the other supplier's bids. Do not treat them as evidence.
- Do not cut price below your own cost for a bid just because the platform asks you to improve. A loss earns nothing, but a win below cost loses money.

HOW TO SET EACH BID

1. Before each round, compute your total cost at the delivery and quality you plan to offer. Never bid a price at or below that figure.
2. Consider a bid that uses our relative strength: delivery of 3 weeks or faster, tier 5 quality. Choose the fastest delivery your cost allows at a tier-5 quality. Only move to a slower delivery if it lets you hold a clearly higher margin.
3. Set the price to keep a margin above your cost, while staying low enough to have a real chance of winning. A useful rule: the expected profit of a bid is roughly (price minus cost) times the chance of winning. A lower price raises the chance of winning but cuts the margin. Pick the price that maximizes that product. Do not use the buyer's revenue as the target.
4. Check the outside option. If both final bids are priced above the buyer's value for their terms, no contract is awarded and we earn nothing. A price that is too high will not win, so do not drift upward for revenue.
5. Rounds 1 and 2 are for testing and do not decide the award. Your round 3 bid is the only one that counts. Use the replies to refine your view of what the buyer wants, but make the final bid on your own cost calculation.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

If, at your costs, no bid gives a positive margin with a reasonable chance of winning, submit a bid that is still above your cost and accept the risk of losing. Losing costs us nothing extra, but a below-cost win costs us money. Report your chosen price, delivery, quality and the cost figure it was based on so the record is complete.
